newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Opposition wins seat in Tunisian by-elections.
newsitem.headline: Opposition wins seat in Tunisian by-elections.

text.p: An opposition candidate won one of the two parliamentary seats in by-elections held in Tunisia on Sunday, official results published on Monday said.

Arbia Ben Ammar Bouchiha, a candidate supported by an alliance between the Party of Popular Unity and the Unionist Democratic Union, won the Ben Arous seat to replace jailed opponent Khemais Chammari.

Chammari, Vice-President of the main opposition party Democratic Socialist's Movement (DMS), lost his seat after a court sentenced him to five years in prison last July for disclosing judicial secrets.
The RCD would have won the Ben Arous seat because of the weakeness of the opposition parties, but apparently decided to leave it in the hands of the opposition.
The candidate of the ruling Constitutional Democratic Rallye Party (RCD), Belgacem Bouaja, won the other seat in the southern city of Medenine against an opposition candidate.
Ben Ammar Bouchiha had campained for Tunisian President Ben Ali and for the protection of environment in the Ben Arous populous industrial area near Tunis.
Results showed she obtained 35 percent of the votes in a competition against three other opposition candidates in which DMS's candidate obtained 32 percent of the votes.

An amendment to the electoral code reserved 19 of the 163 seats in parliament at the March 1994 general elections for legal opposition parties. The next presidential and parliamentarian elections are due in 1999.
